lesson.title: Find a missing rectangle side
lesson.subtitle: P4 measurement revision
lesson.objective: Find a missing length from area or perimeter.
lesson.story: Use the given area and one known side to find the missing width.

steps.title: Choose the measure's unit
steps.prompt: The rectangle has area 84 cm². Which unit names this given measure?
hints: Think about what the measure describes.
Area covers squares; perimeter follows a line.
Length uses cm, area uses cm².

steps.title: Choose a relationship
steps.prompt: A rectangle has height 7 cm and area 84 cm². How can you find the missing width?

choices.label: Divide the area by the length of the side you know.
Subtract the known side from half the perimeter.
Add the area and the known side together.

hints: Area is width × height; perimeter is twice width plus twice height.
Is the measure area or perimeter?

steps.title: Find the missing side
steps.prompt: Find the missing width when a rectangle has height 7 cm and area 84 cm². Give your answer in centimetres.
hints: Write the relationship for the given measure.
Use the known side in the relationship.

steps.title: Explain the measure

choices.label: An inside split line also counts as part of the perimeter.
Area counts square units; perimeter is only the outside edge.
Area and perimeter are both measured in the same units.

hints: Look at what is being measured.
Area covers a surface; perimeter goes around its boundary.
An inside teaching split is not an outside edge.
Choose the explanation that separates square units from boundary length.
